questions.question: PQ is a diameter of a circle and PS is a chord. If PQ is 82 cm and PS is 80 cm, the distance (in cm) of PS from the center of the circle is:
questions.questionHtml: PQ is a diameter of a circle and PS is a chord. If PQ is 82 cm and PS is 80 cm, the distance (in cm) of PS from the center of the circle is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Diameter of the circle, PQ = 82 cm

Chord of the circle, PS = 80 cm

Formula Used:

Using the right triangle property in a circle:

If a chord is perpendicular to the diameter, the formula to find the distance from the center to the chord is:

Distance = \(\sqrt{r^2 - (c/2)^2}\)

Where, r = radius of the circle, c = length of the chord

Calculation:

Radius, r = PQ / 2 = 82 / 2 = 41 cm

Half of the chord, c/2 = 80 / 2 = 40 cm

Distance from the center = \(\sqrt{41^2 - 40^2}\)

Distance = \(\sqrt{1681 - 1600}\)

Distance = \(\sqrt{81}\)

Distance = 9 cm

The distance of PS from the center of the circle is 9 cm.

questions.question: In the given figure, O is the centre of the circle. If ∠BAO = 30° and ∠BCO = 50°, then ∠AOC is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: In the given figure, O is the centre of the circle. If ∠BAO = 30° and ∠BCO = 50°, then ∠AOC is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

As shown in the given circle O is the center of the circle

∠BAO = 30° and ∠BCO = 50°  ______ ( 1 )

Let us consider the full triangle as shown in the above figure.

Calculation:

Let us consider the Δ AOC,

Let ∠OAC = ∠OCA = x°

As sum of all angles of a triangle = 180°

⇒ ∠AOC + x° + x° = 180°

⇒ ∠AOC = 180° - 2x° _______ ( 2 )

Now, in Δ BAC also

⇒ ∠ABC + ∠BAC + ∠BCA = 180°

∠ABC + 30° + x° + 50° + x° = 180°

∠ABC + 80° + 2x° = 180°

⇒  ∠ABC = 180° - 80° - 2x°

⇒ ∠ABC = 100° - 2x° ______ ( 3 )

Theorem used:

As angle made a chord on any point on a circle = ( Angle made by the same chord on the centre )/2

∴ ∠ABC = (∠AOC/2)

⇒ 100° - 2x° = ( 180° - 2x° )/2

⇒ 100° - 2x° = 90° - x°

⇒ x° = 10°

Now in Δ AOC , ∠AOC = 180° - 2x° ( from ( 2 ) )

∠AOC = 180° - 2× 10° = 160°

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, AD is a diameter and AC is a chord. Point B is on AC such that OB = 7 cm and ∠OBA= 60°. If ∠DOC = 60°, then what is the length of BC (in cm)?
questions.questionHtml: In a circle with centre O, AD is a diameter and AC is a chord. Point B is on AC such that OB = 7 cm and ∠OBA= 60°. If ∠DOC = 60°, then what is the length of BC (in cm)?
questions.solution:
Given:

AD is a diameter

OB = 7 cm

∠OBA= 60° and ∠DOC = 60° 

Calculation:

∠ACD = 90° (inscribed angle by diameter)

In ΔOCD, OC = OD = Radius and ∠DOC = 60°

⇒ ΔOCD is an isosceles triangle

⇒ ∠OCD = ∠ODC = (180° - 60°)/2 = 60°

∠ACO = ∠BCO = ​∠ACD - ∠OCD = 90° - 60° = 30° 

∠OBA = ∠BOC + ∠BCO          ----(External Angle)

⇒ ∠BOC = 60° - 30° = 30° 

In ΔOBC

∠BOC = ∠BCO = 30° 

⇒ OB = BC 

⇒ BC = 7cm

∴ The length of BC is 7 cm.

questions.question: PAQ is a tangent to a circle with centre O, at a point A on it. AB is a chord such that ∠BAQ = x° (x < 90°). C is a point on the major arc AB such that ∠ACB = y°. If ∠ABO = 32°, then the value of x + y is:
questions.questionHtml: PAQ is a tangent to a circle with centre O, at a point A on it. AB is a chord such that ∠BAQ = x° (x < 90°). C is a point on the major arc AB such that ∠ACB = y°. If ∠ABO = 32°, then the value of x + y is:
questions.solution:
∠ABO = 32°, ∠BAQ = X and ∠ACB = Y

∠ABO = ∠BAO = 32° [OA = OB]

∠OAQ = 90° [tangent]

∠OAQ = ∠BAO + ∠BAQ

⇒ 90° = 32° + x

⇒ x = 90° - 32° = 58°

∠BAQ = X and ∠ACB = Y are on same arc, hence

⇒ ∠BAQ = ∠ACB 

⇒ x = y = 58°

⇒ x + y = 58° + 58°

⇒ x + y = 116°

questions.question: AB and CD are two chords of a circle that intersects at E inside the circle. If ∠BEC = 125° and ∠EBD = 28°, then what is the measure of ∠BAC?
questions.questionHtml: AB and CD are two chords of a circle that intersects at E inside the circle. If ∠BEC = 125° and ∠EBD = 28°, then what is the measure of ∠BAC?
questions.solution:
Given:

∠BEC = 125° and ∠EBD = 28° 

Calculation:

∠BEC + ∠BED = 180°.... ( linear pairs are complimentary)

⇒ 125° + ∠BED = 180°

⇒ ∠BED = 55°

In ΔDEB ,

∠DEB + ∠EBD + ∠BDE = 180° .....(Angle sum property)

⇒ 55° + 28° + ∠BDE = 180°

⇒83° + ∠BDE = 180°

⇒ ∠BDE = 97°

∠ BDE = ∠ BDC

Same segment theorem,

∠BAC = ∠BDC

⇒ ∠BAC = ∠BDC = 97°

∴ The measure of ∠BAC is 97°

questions.question: The perimeter of a minor sector of a circle of radius 5 cm is 15.5 cm. Find the area of the minor sector (use π = \(\frac{22}{7}\) ).
questions.questionHtml: The perimeter of a minor sector of a circle of radius 5 cm is 15.5 cm. Find the area of the minor sector (use π = \(\frac{22}{7}\)).
questions.solution:
Perimeter of minor sector = 2 × radius + length of cord  ⇒ 2 × 5 + length of cord = 15.5 ⇒ Length of cord = 15.5 - 10 = 5.5 cm  

Area of minor sector = (1/2) × radius ×  length of cord ⇒ (1/2) × 5 × 5.5 ⇒ 27.5/2 = 13.75 cm2

questions.question: PQ is a chord of a circle. The tangent XR at point X on the circle intersects the extension of PQ at point R. Given that XR = 12 cm, PQ = x cm, and QR = (x - 2) cm, find the value of x.
questions.questionHtml: PQ is a chord of a circle. The tangent XR at point X on the circle intersects the extension of PQ at point R. Given that XR = 12 cm, PQ = x cm, and QR = (x - 2) cm, find the value of x.
questions.solution:
122 = (2x - 2)(x - 2), ⇒ 144 = 2x(x - 2) - 2(x - 2)

⇒ 144 = 2x2 - 6x + 4, ⇒ 2x2 - 6x - 140 = 0

⇒ x2 - 3x - 70 = 0, ⇒ (x - 10)(x + 7) = 0

⇒ x = 10 (since length must be positive).

questions.question: Two circles of radii 18 cm and 12 cm intersect each other and the length of their common chord is 16 cm. Then what is the distance (in cm) between their centres?
questions.questionHtml: Two circles of radii 18 cm and 12 cm intersect each other and the length of their common chord is 16 cm. Then what is the distance (in cm) between their centres?
questions.solution:
Given:

The Radii of the two circles are 18 cm and 12 cm.

The length of their common chord is 16 cm.

Concept used:

A line that is drawn perpendicular to the chord from the center of a circle always bisects the chord.

H2 = B2 + P2

Calculation:

At first join O, P and A 

Now, OBA is a right angle triangle and PBA is also a right angle triangle.

Length of AB = AC/2 = 16/2 = 8 cm.

Again, OB2 = 182 – 82 = 260

⇒ OB = √260 = 2√65  

And BP2 = 122 – 82 = 80

⇒ BP = 4√5

Now distance between their centres is OP = OB + BP

⇒ OP = 2√65 + 4√5

⇒ OP = 2√5(2 + √13)

∴ Distance (in cm) between their centers is  2√5(2 + √13)

questions.question: Two circles intersect each other such that each passes through the centre of other. Radius of these circles are equal. If the length of common chord is 14 \(\sqrt3\) cm, then what will be the sum of circumferences of these two circles?
questions.questionHtml: Two circles intersect each other such that each passes through the centre of other. Radius of these circles are equal. If the length of common chord is 14\(\sqrt3\) cm, then what will be the sum of circumferences of these two circles?
questions.solution:
Let the radius be r cm. and AP = PB = 7√3

OO' = r, again O'A = OA = r [Radius of the circle]

∠APO' = 90°, then O'P = PO = r/2

In the ΔAOO', from Pythagoras theorem, (AO')2 = (O'P)2 + (AP)2

⇒ r2 = (r/2)2 + (7√3)2 ⇒ r2 = r2/4 + 147 ⇒ 3r2/4 = 147 ⇒ r = 7 × 2 = 14 cm

Circumference of the two circles ⇒ 2 × 2 × 22/7 × 14 ⇒ 176 cm

questions.question: The centers of two circles of radii 25 cm and 35 cm are 80 cm apart. What is the ratio of the lengths of the transverse common tangent to the direct common tangent to these circles?
questions.questionHtml: The centers of two circles of radii 25 cm and 35 cm are 80 cm apart. What is the ratio of the lengths of the transverse common tangent to the direct common tangent to these circles?
questions.solution:
r1 = 25 cm, r2 = 35 cm, d = 80 cm.

Direct common tangent: D = √(d² - (r₁ - r₂)²)

= √(80² - 10²) = √(6400 - 100) = √6300 cm.

Transverse common tangent: T = √(d² - (r₁ + r₂)²)

= √(80² - 60²) = √(6400 - 3600) = √2800 cm.

Ratio: T / D = √2800 : √6300 = √(2800/6300) = √(28/63) = √4/9 = 2/3 = 2 : 3

questions.question: AB is a chord of a circle with centre O, while PAQ is the tangent at A.R is a point on the minor arc AB. If ∠BAQ = 70 °, then find the measure of ∠ ARB .
questions.questionHtml: AB is a chord of a circle with centre O, while PAQ is the tangent at A.R is a point on the minor arc AB. If ∠BAQ = 70°, then find the measure of ∠ARB .
questions.solution:
Δ OBA, ∠BOA = 180º – (∠OBA + ∠OAB) ⇒ ∠BOA = 180º – (20º + 20º) = 180º - 40º = 140º

∠BOA (exterior angle) = 360º – 140º = 220º

∠ARB = \(1\over 2\) × (220º) = 110º

questions.question: The vertices of a Δ ABC lie on a circle with centre O. AO is produced to meet the circle at the point P. D is a point on BC such that AD ⊥ BC. If ∠B = 68° and ∠C = 52°, then the measure of ∠DAP is:
questions.questionHtml: The vertices of a Δ ABC lie on a circle with centre O. AO is produced to meet the circle at the point P. D is a point on BC such that AD ⊥ BC. If ∠B = 68° and ∠C = 52°, then the measure of ∠DAP is:
questions.solution:
Given:

AD ⊥ BC

∠B = 68° 

∠C = 52° 

Calculation:

Join O to B where point O is the circum centre of the triangle.

⇒ ∠BOA = 2∠BCA

⇒ 2 × 52° 

⇒ 104° 

In ΔBOA

⇒ OB = OA [radius of the circle]

⇒ ∠OBA = ∠OAB

⇒ ∠AOB + ∠OAB + ∠OBA = 180° 

⇒ 2∠OAB = (180° – 104°)

⇒ 2∠OAB = 76° 

⇒ ∠OAB = (76/2)

⇒ ∠OAB = 38° 

In ΔABD

⇒ ∠ABD + ∠BDA + ∠DAB = 180° 

⇒ ∠DAB = (180° – 90° – 68°)

⇒ ∠DAB = 22° 

Now,

∠DAP = ∠BAO – ∠BAD 

⇒ ∠DAP = (38° – 22°)

⇒ ∠DAP = 16° 

So, the required value is 16°

questions.question: AB is the diameter of a circle with centre O. C and D are two points on the circumference of the circle on either side of AB, such that ∠CAB = 42° and ∠ABD = 57°. What is difference (in degrees) between the measures of ∠CAD and ∠CBD?
questions.questionHtml: AB is the diameter of a circle with centre O. C and D are two points on the circumference of the circle on either side of AB, such that ∠CAB = 42° and ∠ABD = 57°. What is difference (in degrees) between the measures of ∠CAD and ∠CBD?
questions.solution:
∠ACB = 90° [∵ AB is diameter]

So, in ΔACB, ∠CBA = (180° - ∠ACB - ∠CAB) ⇒ ∠CBA = (180° - 90° - 42°) ⇒ ∠CBA = 48°

So, ∠CBD = (∠CBA + ∠ABD) ⇒ ∠CBD = (48° + 57°) ⇒ ∠CBD = 105°

Again, ADBC is a cyclic quadrilateral so, ∠CAD = (180° - ∠CBD) ⇒ ∠CAD = (180° - 105°) ⇒ ∠CAD = 75°

Difference = 105° - 75° ⇒ 30°

questions.question: AB and BC are two chords of a circle with centre O. Both chords are on either side of the centre O. Point A and point C are connected to the centre O, such that ∠BAO = 36° and ∠BCO = 48°. What is the degree measure of the angle subtended by the minor arc AC at the centre O?
questions.questionHtml: AB and BC are two chords of a circle with centre O. Both chords are on either side of the centre O. Point A and point C are connected to the centre O, such that ∠BAO = 36° and ∠BCO = 48°. What is the degree measure of the angle subtended by the minor arc AC at the centre O?
questions.solution:
∠OAB = ∠OBA = 36°  (angles opposite to equal sides are equal)

⇒ ∠OCB = ∠OBC = 48°

⇒ ∠ABC = ∠OBC + ∠OBA = 48° + 36° = 84°

The angle subtended by the minor arc AC at the centre O = ∠AOC ⇒ ∠AOC = 2 × 84 = 168

questions.question: AB is a diameter of a circle. C and D are points on the opposite sides of the diameter AB, such that ∠ACD = 25°. E is a point on the minor arc BD. Find the measure of ∠BED (in degrees).
questions.questionHtml: AB is a diameter of a circle. C and D are points on the opposite sides of the diameter AB, such that ∠ACD = 25°. E is a point on the minor arc BD. Find the measure of ∠BED (in degrees).
questions.solution:
Given:

∠ACD = 25° 

Calculation:

 

AB is the diameter of the circle.

∠ACD = 25° 

∠ACD = ∠ABD = 25° (Angles formed on the same arc are equal.)

∠ADB = 90° (Angle formed by diameter in a semicircle)

In Δ ADB

∠BAD = 180° - (∠ADB + ∠ABD)

⇒ 180° - (90° + 25°) = 65° 

∴ ∠BAD = 65° 

Now, In quadrilateral ABED,

∠BAD + ∠BED = 180° (Sum of opposite angles are 180°)

⇒ 65° + ∠BED = 180° 

⇒ ∠BED = 180° - 65° = 115° 

∴ The measure of ∠BED is 115°.

questions.question: Two circles having equal radius intersect each other such that each passes through the centre of the other. Length of the common chord is 24 cm , then what will be the diameter of each circle?
questions.questionHtml: Two circles having equal radius intersect each other such that each passes through the centre of the other. Length of the common chord is 24 cm, then what will be the diameter of each circle?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For two equal circles passing through each other's centers, the common chord length is given by: L = √3 × r.

⇒ 24 = √3 × r

⇒ r = 24 / √3 = 8√3 cm

⇒ Diameter of the circle (d) = 2 × r = 2 × 8√3

⇒ d = 16√3 cm

∴ The correct answer is 16√3 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of both circles = r cm

Length of the common chord (AB) = 24 cm

Formula Used:

In a triangle, the line joining the centers of two circles is the perpendicular bisector of their common chord. Pythagoras theorem: Hypotenuse2 = Base2 + Perpendicular2.

Calculations:

Let O1 and O2 be the centers of the two circles.

⇒ O1O2 = Radius (r) (since each passes through the other's center)

⇒ In ΔO1MA, where M is the midpoint of AB and O1O2:

⇒ AM = AB ÷ 2 = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm

⇒ O1M = O1O2 ÷ 2 = r ÷ 2

⇒ O1A = Radius = r

⇒ Using Pythagoras theorem: O1A2 = O1M2 + AM2

⇒ r2 = (r/2)2 + 122

⇒ r2 − r2/4 = 144

⇒ 3r2 / 4 = 144

⇒ r2 = (144 × 4) ÷ 3 = 48 × 4 = 192

⇒ r = √192 = 8√3 cm

⇒ Diameter = 2 × r = 2 × 8√3 = 16√3 cm

∴ The correct answer is 16√3 cm.

Additional Information

Common Chord Property

The line joining the centers of two intersecting circles is the perpendicular bisector of their common chord.

Intersecting Equal Circles

When two equal circles pass through each other's centers, they form two equilateral triangles with the intersection points and the centers, all sides being equal to the radius r.

Common Chord Length Formula

If two circles of radii r1 and r2 have centers at distance d, the length of the common chord is 2 × √[r12 − ((r12 − r22 + d2) ÷ 2d)2].

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, PAX and PBY are the tangents to the circle at points A and B, from an external point P. Q is any point on the circle such that ∠QAX = 59° and ∠QBY = 72°. What is the measure of ∠AQB?
questions.questionHtml: In a circle with centre O, PAX and PBY are the tangents to the circle at points A and B, from an external point P. Q is any point on the circle such that ∠QAX = 59° and ∠QBY = 72°. What is the measure of ∠AQB?

questions.question: Points P, Q, R, S and T lie in this order on a circle with centre O. If chord TS is parallel to diameter PR and ∠RQT= 58°, then find the measure (in degrees) of ∠RTS.
questions.questionHtml: Points P, Q, R, S and T lie in this order on a circle with centre O. If chord TS is parallel to diameter PR and ∠RQT= 58°, then find the measure (in degrees) of ∠RTS.
questions.solution:
Given:

Points P, Q, R, S and T lie in this order on a circle with centre O

chord TS is parallel to diameter PR

∠RQT = 58° 

Calculation:

PR is a diameter

∠PTR = 90° .....(angle inscribe in a semicircle)

also ∠TPR = 58°   .....(angle formed on same chord)

so, ∠PRT = 180° - ∠PTR – ∠TPR

⇒ ∠PRT = 180° - 90° - 58°

⇒ ∠PRT = 32° 

∠PRT = ∠RTS = 32°   (Alternate interior angle as chord TS is parallel to diameter PR)

 

∴ The measure of ∠RTS is 32.

Alternate Method

 

In this figure ∠PQR = 90° 

And ∠PQT = 90° - 58° = 32° 

Now we know angle formed on same chord are equal.

∴ ∠PQT = ∠PRT

And ∠PRT = ∠RTS (Alternate angle) 

∠RTS = 32°

questions.question: The length of the common chord of two intersecting circles is 24 cm. If the diameter of the circles are 30 cm and 26 cm, then the distance between the centres (in cm) is:
questions.questionHtml: The length of the common chord of two intersecting circles is 24 cm. If the diameter of the circles are 30 cm and 26 cm, then the distance between the centres (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
Shown above are the two intersecting circles with AB the common chord.

⇒ AO = AB/2 = 24/2 = 12 cm

AX and AY are the radius of the respective circles.

⇒ Hence, AX = 26/2 = 13 cm and AY = 30/2 = 15 cm

ΔAOX and ΔAOY are right-angled triangles

Hence, AX2 = AO2 + OX2 and AY2 = AO2 + OY2 ⇒ OX2 = 132 – 122 and OY2 = 152 - 122

⇒ OX2 = 25 and OY2 = 81 Hence, OX = 5 and OY = 9

⇒ XY = OX + OY ⇒ XY = 9 + 5 ⇒ XY = 14

questions.question: The distance between the centres of two circles is 81 cm, and their radii are 42 cm and 51 cm. What is the length (in cm) of the direct common tangent to the circles?
questions.questionHtml: The distance between the centres of two circles is 81 cm, and their radii are 42 cm and 51 cm. What is the length (in cm) of the direct common tangent to the circles?
questions.solution:

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, a diameter AB is produced to a point P lying outside the circle and PT is a tangent to the circle at a point C on it. If ∠BPT = 28°, then what is the measure of ∠BCP?
questions.questionHtml: In a circle with centre O, a diameter AB is produced to a point P lying outside the circle and PT is a tangent to the circle at a point C on it. If ∠BPT = 28°, then what is the measure of ∠BCP?

Given:

AB has been extended to P.

PT is the tangent at C.

∠BPT = 28°

Concept used:

The tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.

Calculation:

OC⊥PT at C

So, ΔOCP is a right-angled triangle at C.

Here, OA = OB = Radii of the circle

Here, ABP is a straight line.

⇒ ∠BCP = 180° - 28° - 121° 

⇒ ∠BCP = 31°

questions.question: ΔABC is drawn in a circle such that AC = BC and ∠BAC = 65°. From points B and C two tangents are drawn which intersect at point P. What is the measure of ∠BPC?
questions.questionHtml: ΔABC is drawn in a circle such that AC = BC and ∠BAC = 65°. From points B and C two tangents are drawn which intersect at point P. What is the measure of ∠BPC?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

By the Alternate Segment Theorem, the angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle subtended by that chord in the alternate segment.

⇒ ∠PBC = ∠BAC = 65°

⇒ ∠PCB = ∠BAC = 65°

In ΔBPC, the sum of all interior angles is 180°:

⇒ ∠BPC + 65° + 65° = 180°

⇒ ∠BPC = 180° − 130° = 50°

∴ The correct answer is 50°.

Alternate Method

Given:

ΔABC is inscribed in a circle with center O.

AC = BC and ∠BAC = 65°.

Tangents at B and C meet at external point P.

Calculations:

⇒ The angle subtended by chord BC at the circumference is ∠BAC = 65°.

⇒ The angle subtended by an arc at the center is exactly double the angle subtended at the circumference.

⇒ Central Angle ∠BOC = 2 × ∠BAC = 2 × 65° = 130°.

⇒ The radius drawn to the point of contact is directly perpendicular to the tangent line.

⇒ Therefore, ∠OBP = 90° and ∠OCP = 90°.

⇒ In quadrilateral OBPC, the sum of all internal angles is strictly 360°.

⇒ ∠BOC + ∠OBP + ∠BPC + ∠OCP = 360°

⇒ 130° + 90° + ∠BPC + 90° = 360°

⇒ 310° + ∠BPC = 360°

⇒ ∠BPC = 360° − 310° = 50°

∴ The correct answer is 50°.

Additional Information

Alternate Segment Theorem

The angle between a tangent line and a chord passing through the point of contact is perfectly equal to the angle subtended by that same chord in the alternate segment of the circle.

Angle Between Intersecting Tangents

The angle between two distinct tangents drawn from an external given point to a circle is supplementary to the central angle subtended by the chord connecting their respective points of contact (∠P + ∠O = 180°).

Inscribed Angle Theorem

The angle strictly subtended by an arc at the center is mathematically double the angle subtended by it at any remaining part of the circle's circumference.

questions.question: Points A, B and C are on a circle with centre O such that ∠BOC = 84°. If AC is produced to a point D such that ∠ BDC = 40°, then find the measure of ∠ ABD (in degrees).
questions.questionHtml: Points A, B and C are on a circle with centre O such that ∠BOC = 84°. If AC is produced to a point D such that ∠BDC = 40°, then find the measure of ∠ABD (in degrees).
questions.solution:
Given:

Points A, B, and C are on a circle with centre O.

∠BOC = 84°

AC is produced to a point D.

∠BDC = 40°

Concept used:

By the inscribed angle theorem, the measure of an inscribed angle is half the measure of the intercepted arc.

The sum of all angles of a triangle is 180°.

Calculation:

Now, ∠BAC = (84 ÷ 2)° = 42°

So, ∠BDC = 40° = ∠BDA

So, from  ΔBAD,

∠BAD + ∠BDA + ∠ABD = 180°

⇒ 42° + 40° + ∠ABD = 180°

⇒ ∠ABD = 180° - (42° + 40°)

⇒ ∠ABD = 98°

questions.question: AB is a chord of a circle with centre O and P is any point on the circle. If ∠APB = 122°, then what is the measure of ∠OAB ?
questions.questionHtml: AB is a chord of a circle with centre O and P is any point on the circle. If ∠APB = 122°, then what is the measure of ∠OAB ?
questions.solution:
Given:

∠APB = 122° 

Concept used:

Sum of opposite sides of a cyclic quadrilateral are 180°

The angle subtended by an arc of a circle at its center is twice the angle it subtends anywhere on the circle’s circumference.

Calculation:

In the given figure,

APBT is a cyclic quadrilateral.

∠ATB + ∠APB = 180° [sum of opposite angles are 180°]

⇒ x° + 122° = 180° 

⇒ x = (180° – 122°)

⇒ x = 58° 

∠ATB = 58° 

And we know that the angle subtended by an arc of a circle at its center is twice the angle it subtends anywhere on the circle’s circumference.

⇒ ∠AOB = 2 × ∠ATB

⇒ ∠AOB = 2 × 58° 

⇒ ∠AOB = 116° 

Now,

OA = OB [radius of the circle]

Then,

∠OAB + ∠AOB + ∠OBA = 180° 

⇒ θ + 116° + θ = 180° 

⇒ 2θ + 116° = 180° 

⇒ 2θ = (180° – 116°)

⇒ 2θ = 64° 

⇒ θ = 32° 

so,

∠OAB = θ = 32° 

∴ The required value of ∠OAB is 32°.

Shortcut Trick 

From the above given diagram we have

⇒ θ = P - 90°

⇒ θ = 122° - 90° = 32°

∴ The correct answer is 32°.

Centre O

Line RS and Line OP intersect each other  ⇒ \(\angle\)RTO = ​​\(\angle\)STP

questions.question: The diameter PQ of a circle with centre O is perpendicular to the chord RS. PQ intersects RS at T. If RS = 16 cm and QT = 4 cm, what is the length (in cm) of the diameter of the circle?
questions.questionHtml: The diameter PQ of a circle with centre O is perpendicular to the chord RS. PQ intersects RS at T. If RS = 16 cm and QT = 4 cm, what is the length (in cm) of the diameter of the circle?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When a diameter is perpendicular to a chord, it bisects the chord: RT = TS = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm.

According to the Intersecting Chords Theorem, RT × TS = PT × TQ.

⇒ 8 × 8 = PT × 4

⇒ PT = 64 ÷ 4 = 16 cm.

⇒ Diameter PQ = PT + TQ = 16 + 4 = 20 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 20 cm.

Alternate Method

Given: Chord RS = 16 cm, PQ ⊥ RS at T, QT = 4 cm.

Formula Used: Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse2 = Base2 + Perpendicular2

⇒ Let the radius of the circle be r cm.

⇒ In ▵OTR, OR is the radius, so OR = r.

⇒ Since PQ is the diameter, OQ = r. Given QT = 4 cm, OT = OQ − QT = r − 4.

⇒ RS is bisected by the diameter at T, so RT = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm.

⇒ By Pythagoras Theorem in ▵OTR: OR2 = OT2 + RT2

⇒ r2 = (r − 4)2 + 82

⇒ r2 = r2 − 8r + 16 + 64

⇒ 8r = 80

⇒ r = 10 cm

⇒ Diameter = 2 × r = 2 × 10 = 20 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 20 cm.

Additional Information

Perpendicular from Center

A perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to a chord always bisects the chord into two equal segments.

Intersecting Chords Theorem

For two chords intersecting at a point T inside a circle, the product of the segments of one chord equals the product of the segments of the other: AT × TB = CT × TD.

Radius and Diameter

The diameter is the longest chord of a circle and its length is exactly twice the length of the radius (D = 2r).

Also, AC = √[502 - (7 - 7)2] ⇒ AC = √(2500 - 0) = √2500 = 50 cm

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, PQ, and QR are two chords such that ∠PQR = 118°. What is the measure of ∠OPR?
questions.questionHtml: In a circle with centre O, PQ, and QR are two chords such that ∠PQR = 118°. What is the measure of ∠OPR?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For any triangle OPR inscribed in a circle with center O and chords PQ and QR forming an angle θ:

Measure of ∠OPR = |∠PQR − 90°|

⇒ ∠OPR = |118° − 90°|

⇒ ∠OPR = 28°

∴ The correct answer is 28°.

Alternate Method

Given: ∠PQR = 118° in a circle with centre O.

Formula Used: Angle at the center is twice the angle at the circumference. In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles sum to 180°.

⇒ Let S be a point on the major arc PR. Then PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral.

⇒ ∠PSR + ∠PQR = 180°

⇒ ∠PSR + 118° = 180°

⇒ ∠PSR = 62°

⇒ Central angle subtended by arc PR is ∠POR = 2 × ∠PSR

⇒ ∠POR = 2 × 62° = 124°

⇒ In ▵OPR, OP = OR (radii of the same circle).

⇒ ▵OPR is an isosceles triangle, so ∠OPR = ∠ORP.

⇒ ∠OPR + ∠ORP + ∠POR = 180°

⇒ 2 × ∠OPR + 124° = 180°

⇒ 2 × ∠OPR = 56°

⇒ ∠OPR = 28°

∴ The correct answer is 28°.

Additional Information

Angle at Center Theorem

The angle subtended by an arc at the center is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circumference.

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

The sum of the opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is always 180° (∠A + ∠C = 180°).

Isosceles Triangle in Circles

Any triangle formed by two radii and a chord is an isosceles triangle because radii of the same circle are equal in length.

questions.question: The radii of two concentric circles are 34 cm and 50 cm. A and D are the points on larger circle and B and C are points on smaller circle. If ABCD is a straight line and BC = 32 cm, then what is the length of AD?

Similarly, in ΔOPD, ⇒ OD2 = OP2 + PD2 ⇒ 502 = 302 + PD2 ⇒ PD2 = 2500 - 900 ⇒ PD = 40 cm

So, AD = (2 × PD) = (2 × 40) = 80 cm

questions.question: In a circle with center O, the diameter AB extended to the point C, outside the circle. CD is a tangent at the point D on the circle. If the radius of circle is 6 cm and ∠DBC = 120°, then the length of CD is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: In a circle with center O, the diameter AB extended to the point C, outside the circle. CD is a tangent at the point D on the circle. If the radius of circle is 6 cm and ∠DBC = 120°, then the length of CD is equal to:
questions.solution:
Radius of circle (OD = OB = OA) = 6 cm, ∠DBC = 120°

Angle between tangent and radius at the point of contact = 90° (∠ODC = 90°)

Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°

∠OBD + ∠DBC = 180° (angles in a straight line) ⇒ ∠OBD + 120° = 180°

∠OBD = 180° - 120° = 60°

In triangle OBD, OB = OD (radii of the same circle) ⇒ ∠ODB = ∠OBD = 60°

In triangle OBD, ∠BOD + ∠OBD + ∠ODB = 180° (sum of angles in a triangle)

∠BOD + 60° + 60° = 180° ⇒ ∠BOD = 180° - 120° = 60°

Since all angles in triangle OBD are 60°, triangle OBD is an equilateral triangle.

Therefore, OB = OD = BD = 6 cm.

Using trigonometry in right-angled triangle ODC:

tan(∠DOC) = CD / OD ⇒ tan(60°) = CD / 6

\(\sqrt{3}\) = CD / 6 ⇒ CD = 6\(\sqrt{3}\) cm

∴ The length of CD is \(6\sqrt{3}\) cm.
